facts.statement: The genus Gymnotrachelus was described by Dunkel and Bungart in 1939.
Gymnotrachelus lived during the Late Devonian period, specifically the Famennian stage.
Fossils of Gymnotrachelus date from 365.2 to 358.86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Famennian (365.2 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: The only known fossils of Gymnotrachelus come from the Late Famennian Cleveland Shale in Ohio.
facts.quote: known from the Late Famennian Cleveland Shale of Ohio

facts.statement: Gymnotrachelus is an extinct genus containing a single species of large selenosteid arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Gymnotrachelus is an extinct monospecific genus of large selenosteid arthrodire placoderm

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Gymnotrachelus hydei.
facts.quote: The type species is Gymnotrachelus hydei

facts.statement: Gymnotrachelus belongs to the family Selenosteidae within the clade Aspinothoracidi.
facts.quote: Gymnotrachelus is a member of the family Selenosteidae of the clade Aspinothoracidi

facts.statement: Gymnotrachelus is classified in the class Placodermi.
A 2022 study by Jobbins et al. identified Gymnotrachelus as an outgroup to the genera Heintzichthys and Gorgonichthys.
facts.quote: According to a 2022 Jobbins et al. study, Gymnotrachelus was found to be an outgroup to Heintzichthys and Gorgonichthys
